title: Newly appearing links concentrated around hubs in three news narratives
summary: In language-model maps of coverage of three news events, 44% to 51% of next-day emerging links touched an entity in the top tenth by network degree. A ranking based on endpoint degree beat a historical-link baseline on these emerging links, and the margin shrank when high-degree entities were removed.
ai_technology: Claude Haiku, GPT-4.1 and Gemini semantic edge extraction

evidence.tested: The retrospective comparison covered the Canadian Freedom Convoy, Hurricane Melissa and the 2025–26 Iranian protests. It used rolling windows and three separate language-model extractors.
evidence.unknown: The graphs use model-extracted relations without human gold labels. Candidate negatives were sampled randomly, favoring degree-based rankings. The result describes links represented in coverage of three events.
evidence.ai_role: Language models resolved references and extracted semantic relations from each article, which supplied the networks used to quantify where next-day links appeared.
